met_analysis:
The cyclonic storm “Arnab” [Pronunciation :Ornab] over Westcentral and adjoining Eastcentral Bay of Bengal moved west-northwestwards with a speed of 17 kmph during past 6 hours, intensified into a severe cyclonic storm and lies centered at 1730 hrs IST of today, the 26th October, 2026 over Westcentral Bay of Bengal near latitude 15.6°N and longitude 87.3°E, 490 km south-southeast of Gopalpur (Odisha), 490 km east-southeast of Vishakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 560 km east-southeast of Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh), 660 km east of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 730 km east of Bapatla (Andhra Pradesh) and 730 km northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman Islands). It is very likely to continue to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm over the same region during next 12 hours. It is very likely to continue to move west-northwestwards till evening of 27th October and thereafter, it is very likely to move northwestwards and cross Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam as a very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 115-125 kmph gusting to 140 kmph by forenoon of 28th October, 2026
The Low Pressure areaover Southwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining south coastal Tamil Nadu persisted over the same region at 1730 hrs IST of today, the 26th October, 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation extends upto 7.6 km above mean sea level.
The trough from Lakshadweep Area to the cyclonic circulation associated with the low pressure area over Southwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining south coastal Tamil Nadu across South Kerala extending upto 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over north Haryana between 3.1 & 4.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhood at 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The Western Disturbance as a trough in middle & upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along Long. 72°E to the north of Lat. 25°N. it is likely to affect northwest India from the night of 27th October, 2026.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over southeast Uttar Pradesh & adjoining Bihar and extends upto 3.1 km above mean sea level.
